subject: Proposal: Route fingerprint scorecard + exception playbook for Console
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: Route fingerprint scorecard + exception playbook for Console

Team —

Quick summary: after the last runbook review, ACME flagged that they need a single per-route "fingerprint" in Console that captures cost, p50/p95 latency, tail-call profile, and a short list of probable causes + suggested mitigations. They called it a "scorecard" and want it surfaced in the tenant drill and the inspector UI.

I sketched a spec (attached) that:
- defines a compact set of metrics and normalized score (0-100)
- proposes a lightweight exception playbook when score < 45 (auto-suggested mitigations)
- shows sampling and CV thresholds for triggering full traceback exports

Asks:
1) Product: agree on the score cardinality and where we surface it in Console (route tile vs inspector).
2) Analytics: confirm signals we can reliably compute (cost-per-call, cached prefix hit, kv-cache hit rate, seq length distribution).
3) Runtime/Infra: check feasibility for adding the score to existing route metadata without adding large telemetry ingress.

I attached a small sample CSV from ACME's tenant (sanitized) that motivated the exceptions.

Can we sync tomorrow 10:30am PT for a 30m decision + action owners? If that window doesn't work, propose alternatives.

Thanks —
Priyom
Product Manager, Inference Console
Redwood Inference

Attachments: route-scorecard-spec.pdf (spec draft), sample-tenant-slices.csv (sanitized sample)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: Route fingerprint scorecard + exception playbook for Console

Priyom —

Thanks for the clear spec. Quick notes from infra/analytics perspective:
- Signals: we can compute cost-per-call and token-path percentiles from existing ingest. KV-cache hit rate is available but noisy for some legacy routes; we should mark that as "best-effort".
- Ingress: adding one numeric score per route per minute (or per aggregation window) is cheap. The heavy part is when a route falls into the "exception" category and we snapshot traces for full traceback — we should gate that with sampling/window rules.
- Suggested change: make the exception snapshot opt-in per-tenant (default: off) and require a min-sample threshold (e.g., >1000 calls/day) so we don't blow storage for low-volume tenants.

I can take point on the sampling thresholds and an initial query for the p50/p95 breakdowns. Marcus, can you comment on storage/ingest cost for the per-minute scoring?

Jonas
Senior Analytics Engineer

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: Route fingerprint scorecard + exception playbook for Console

Jonas + Priyom —

Quick capacity/finance check: adding a compact score (one number + small metadata) to the route index is fine. If we do per-minute for all routes across all tenants, estimate ~120GB/month additional index growth (ballpark). The expensive bit is trace snapshots. If snapshots are only triggered for exceptions and we enforce the >=1000 calls/day rule and 10% snapshot sample, we're looking at ~1.5TB/month for the early adopter cohort — doable but needs a monthly add-on SKU for storage in Dedicated and Private plans.

Two asks from my side:
- Product: confirm a rollout plan with opt-in for Dedicated/Private and default off for Hosted until we have a compression plan.
- Eng: add a flag to the runtime to tag exception snapshots so they are routed to a cold-tier store.

Marcus
Director, Platform Economics

> On Mon, Jun 21, 2027 at 10:05 AM Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com> wrote:

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 08:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: Route fingerprint scorecard + exception playbook for Console

All —

Love the direction. A few product-focused points:
- UI placement: I prefer the inspector-level scorecard (contextual) with an optional compact badge on the route list. That keeps the route list uncluttered.
- Score components: please keep the score explainable (three bullets): Cost, Tail Behavior, and Cache Health. Each should link to the drill that shows the contributing buckets (e.g., "top 5 callchains by cost").
- Exceptions playbook: we should provide 3-4 templated mitigations (e.g., lower max tokens, enable prefix caching, suggest quantized model variant) and a quick toggle to create an action item for the customer's CS rep.

I can draft the UI mock and copy for the mitigations. Marcus — can you give a final number for the storage SKU so we can show pricing to ACME?

Marissa
Product Lead, Observability

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: Route fingerprint scorecard + exception playbook for Console

Thanks for pulling this together. Decision notes and next steps: 

1) Decision: Proceed with the inspector-level scorecard + compact badge on the route list for early adopters.
2) Scope for MVP: compute score at 15-minute aggregation windows; support cost-per-call, p50/p95, kv-cache hit rate (best-effort). Exception snapshots: gated, opt-in per-tenant, and require >=1000 calls/day.
3) Owners: Jonas (analytics) — define queries and alert thresholds; Marcus (platform economics) — storage SKU and cost impact; Marissa (product) — UI mock and mitigations copy; Priyom (PM) — timeline and rollout plan.
4) Timeline: target alpha in Console Canary 1 (internal) by 2027-08-18; beta for early customers (ACME cohort) by 2027-09-15.

Irene — please circulate this summary to the larger Console working group and include the attached spec in the INF-2345 ticket. Priyom: schedule the 8/18 alpha demo and confirm the ACME opt-in list.

Irene Choi
VP, Observability & Product Operations
